name: BQ24392RSER
title: BQ24392: dual SPST USB 2.0 high-speed switch with BCv1.2 charger detection
summary: Two single-pole single-throw switches that connect or isolate the D+ and D- lines between a micro or mini-USB connector and a USB 2.0 high-speed transceiver, together with a charger detector. Running from VBUS alone, it identifies USB Battery Charging 1.2 ports (SDP, CDP, DCP), Apple and TomTom chargers and other non-compliant adapters, then reports on three outputs (CHG_DET, CHG_AL_N, SW_OPEN) whether charging is allowed and at low or high current, and whether the data switch is closed. VBUS withstands -2 V to 28 V, so no external overvoltage protection is needed. A GOOD_BAT input and a dead-battery timer decide whether the switch closes and how long a dead battery may charge. BQ24392RSER is the 10-pin UQFN (RSE), 2.05 mm × 1.55 mm, on a 3000-piece reel.
key_figures: ±4000 V HBM, ±1500 V CDM, ±8000 V IEC contact on DP_CON and DM_CON

notes: An automotive version qualified to Q100, BQ24392-Q1, also exists.

circuits.title: Application schematic
circuits.description: The BQ24392 sits between a micro or mini-USB receptacle and the host transceiver. VBUS, DM_CON and DP_CON each reach the receptacle through a 2.2 Ω ballast resistor; on the receptacle side each line has a low-capacitance ESD diode to ground (1 pF on the data lines, 1 pF to 10 pF on VBUS), and VBUS also carries a 0.1 µF and a 1 µF to 10 µF capacitor. DM_HOST and DP_HOST run straight to the host. The system drives GOOD_BAT and reads SW_OPEN, CHG_AL_N and CHG_DET; the two open-drain flags have 10 kΩ pull-ups to 3.3 V. CHG_DET reaches the system through a diode with a 0.5 V drop, its anode on the system side with a 100 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V, for a 3.3 V system; the diode and that pull-up are optional.

operation.text: The part takes its power only from VBUS, supplied by whatever is plugged into the USB receptacle; that source is expected to follow USB 2.0, 5 V at 500 mA. VBUS tolerates up to 28 V, so no external overvoltage protection is needed. Below the 3.5 V VBUS valid threshold nothing is detected, CHG_AL_N is high impedance and the switch stays open.

After power-up the part waits in an idle state until VBUS passes VVBUS_VALID. It then runs data contact detection (DCD), which times out after 600 ms as BCv1.2 requires. If the attached device is BCv1.2 compliant, a 130 ms debounce follows and then primary detection (SDP or not) and secondary detection (DCP or CDP). Detecting a DCP, SDP or CDP takes at least 130 ms and up to 600 ms. If DCD fails, the part checks the voltages on DP_CON and DM_CON to recognise an Apple or TomTom charger, which typically takes about 600 ms; otherwise it reports no charger. SW_OPEN, CHG_AL_N and CHG_DET change only once detection is complete.

The part has two operating modes, the data switch closed or open. The switches close only when an SDP or CDP is found while GOOD_BAT is high; with GOOD_BAT low, or for any dedicated or proprietary charger, they stay open. SW_OPEN is low while the switches are closed and high impedance while open, so the host can watch it to know the data path state.

When a charger is detected while GOOD_BAT is low, the DBP timer starts (32 min typ, 45 min max). If GOOD_BAT is still low when it runs out, the part stops allowing charge and releases CHG_AL_N to high impedance. Driving GOOD_BAT high after expiry restarts detection and the timer.

CHG_AL_N is open drain and active low; CHG_DET is push-pull and active high. Together they tell the system whether it may charge, and whether at low or high current. The system defines what low and high current mean; with CHG_DET high it might try 2 A, 1.5 A or 1.0 A. To use chargers above 1.5 A the system needs a charger IC that watches VBUS while raising its current and backs off when VBUS starts to sag, settling where VBUS holds.

A USB plug's VBUS and GND contacts are longer than its data contacts, so power arrives before D+ and D- touch. The 130 ms debounce after VBUS valid allows for this. With a very slow insertion the detection time is not bounded: if inserting takes longer than 600 ms, DCD times out and a DCP is reported as a non-standard charger with floating D+ and D-.
The switch carries USB 2.0 high-speed data at 480 Mbps.

VBUS needs two bypass capacitors, 0.1 µF for high frequencies with its lower series inductance and 1 µF to 10 µF for lower frequencies. SW_OPEN and CHG_AL_N need 10 kΩ pull-ups to VDDIO. A 2.2 Ω series resistor on each of VBUS, DM_CON and DP_CON adds ballast that protects the chip. DM_CON and DP_CON each want a 1 pF ESD diode rated for 8 kV IEC contact discharge, and VBUS a 1 pF to 10 pF one with the same rating. The pull-up and diode on CHG_DET are optional and adapt it to a 3.3 V system; the CHG_DET pull-up range is 3.5 V to VVBUS.

Put the VBUS bypass capacitors right at the VBUS pin and keep them away from the D+/D- traces. Match the lengths of the DP and DM traces and keep them to 4 inches at most, or the eye degrades; route them as a 90 Ω differential pair to match the USB cable (90 Ω ±15%). Run them on the layer next to the ground plane, with few vias and corners; open up the clearance around any via, avoid through-hole test points, and replace 90° corners by two 45° turns or an arc. Keep them away from crystals, oscillators, clock sources, switching regulators, mounting holes and magnetics. Stubs should be avoided, and kept under 200 mils where unavoidable. Route over unbroken VCC or GND planes and never across a plane split. A board of four or more layers is advised: signal, solid GND, power, signal, with most signals on the top layer beside the uncut ground plane; where a trace must cross a split, decouple well. Fewer signal vias lower EMI.

In the example placement, the impedance-matched USB traces enter DM_HOST/DP_HOST on one side from the transceiver and leave DM_CON/DP_CON on the other toward the connector. The VBUS ballast resistor and bypass capacitors sit beside pin 9, pull-up resistors beside SW_OPEN, CHG_AL_N and CHG_DET, and vias drop to an inner GND plane and a VBUS plane.

The land pattern is non solder mask defined by preference, with 0.07 mm maximum mask clearance all round; a solder mask defined land uses 0.07 mm minimum mask overlap. The stencil uses the same aperture sizes in 0.1 mm thick foil; laser-cut trapezoidal walls with rounded corners help paste release.
